1.title: The Grower's Annual Work Calendar
1.html:
MonthMain Work
NovemberLeaf fall (chute des feuilles)
December–MarchPruning (taille)
Mid-FebruaryTying and arching (liage et arcure)
AprilSoil management / ploughing (labour – entretien du sol)
April–MayTrellising (palissage)
May–JuneDisease and pest control (traitement des vignes)
July–AugustTrimming (rognage)
September–OctoberHarvest (vendanges)

💡 Although the tools have evolved over the centuries, this rhythm of work has remained largely unchanged since Roman times — the vine's own growth cycle is what truly governs the farming calendar.
2.title: Guyot Double Arch Pruning: The Mainstream Technique of Alsace
2.html:
The main pruning method in Alsace is Guyot double arch pruning (taille Guyot double arcure): during winter dormancy (December to March), the grower keeps one or two fruiting canes (sarment) on each vine, and after pruning, in mid-February, bends the canes into an arch (arcure) and ties them to the wire (liage) — this helps distribute nutrients evenly to every bud along the cane, rather than concentrating them only at the tip.

The pruned canes (sarments) are crushed by the tractor and returned to the soil as a natural source of organic matter.
3.title: Soil Management: From Full Ploughing to Natural Grass Cover
3.html:
Soil management in April was traditionally based on ploughing (labour) to loosen the topsoil, but the recent trend has gradually moved to "managed natural grass cover" (Enherbement Naturel Maîtrisé, ENM) — letting natural vegetation grow in the soil and controlling it by rolling or partial weeding once it reaches about 20 cm in height.

This technique captures the many benefits of grass cover: developing a diverse ground-cover plant community, effectively conserving soil and water, and reducing nitrate loss in autumn and winter — a modern practice balancing environmental sustainability and grape quality.
4.question: What is the main pruning method used in Alsace?
4.options.1: Guyot double arch pruning — one or two fruiting canes kept in winter, bent into an arch and tied in mid-February
4.options.3: No pruning at all, letting the vine grow naturally
